candidates.summary: Known as the Queen of Crime, her murder mysteries have captivated audiences for more than a century
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Полиция или суд сообщили новое развитие по делу.
candidates.lead: Known as the Queen of Crime, her murder mysteries have captivated audiences for more than a century
candidates.evidence_text: The country house in Cheadle that inspired Agatha Christie's work - BBC News Image caption, Agatha Christie wrote 78 crime novels that have sold an estimated 2 billion copies in 44 languages By Jen Dale BBC Radio Manchester Published 47 minutes ago Known as the Queen of Crime, Agatha Christie murder mysteries have captivated audiences for more than a century. But it might come as a surprise to some that many of her stories were inspired by a country house in Cheadle, Greater Manchester. Abney Hall is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds after the Cheadle Civic Society erected an information board in the grounds explaining the novelist's connections. In 1902, Christie first arrived at Abney Hall when she was about 11 years old as her older sister Madge lived at the house after marrying into the wealthy Watts family. Nestled in the village of Cheadle, the gothic building has high-ceilinged rooms, gold chandeliers and a red velvet carpet running down the centre of a large wooden staircase. Outside, there are crosses etched into the stone walls as well as distinctive chimney stacks - no doubt the inspiration for one of her stories The Secret of Chimneys. Image source, Cheadle Civic Society Image caption, Abney Hall and the surrounding gardens forms part of a new heritage trail Trever Evers, from the society, said there were plenty of features to inspire the writer. "You know Abney Hall had it all, it had a waterfall, it had a tunnel under the drive," he said. "She loved the fact that the house had back passageways and staircases that they used to hide from each other." Evers added that the geography of Abney Hall was itself an inspiration. "The 4.50 from Paddington [was] a very famous Miss Marple novel," he said. "That's inspired by the grounds at Abney because in Agatha's day the estate was probably I think 10 times bigger than we know it today and the grounds were circled by two railway lines. "The plot revolves around a murder that happens on a train and the body gets pushed out of the train into the estate of a country house. "The fact that Abney was surrounded by these two railway lines, one of which does curve which forces trains to slow down, that is said to have inspired the storyline for that." How Cheadle's Abney Hall inspired Agatha Christie The country house inspired plots in several of her stories Listen on Sounds However, it was in 1926 that Abney Hall plays its most crucial role for Christie. On 3 December of that year, she famously went missing. It was shortly after her successful novel - The murder of Roger Akroyd - had been published. Whilst there were unproved rumours it was to boost book sales, her grandson Matthew Pritchard told the BBC in 2015 there was a lot going on in her life at that time. "I do fairly strongly believe that what she suffered from is rooted in deep unhappiness," he said. "This all that happened when her husband was in the process of leaving her but her mother died and suddenly her whole world crashed from beneath her. "It can provide unexpected effects on your health and maybe an unconscious desire to go away somewhere and wish you weren't there." Image source, Cheadle Civic Society Image caption, The information board about Agatha Christie is part of the new Cheadle heritage trail The search for Christie was one of the largest in the history of Surrey police. She was found 11 days later more than 200 miles away at a hotel in Harrogate. Her sister Madge went to collect her and brought her back to Abney Hall to recover. Evers said the whole episode was a media frenzy at the time. Christie stayed at the country house over the Christmas period of 1926 to recuperate. She went on to write many more books featuring the detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple, who is named after the local train station. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Cheadle's Abney Hall inspired Agatha Christie Christie died in 1976 at the age of 85, having written more than 80 books. Abney Hall stayed in the Watts family for several generations before being sold and became a town hall. It is now leased as office space but the public can access the gardens anytime. The hall is accessible on heritage open days and forms part of the Cheadle heritage trail. candidates.evidence_text: Protests and profits: 25 Years of Manchester's second runway - BBC News Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, The second runway became operational in 2001 By Judy Hobson , North West Tonight and Jenny Coleman , North West Published 43 minutes ago When Manchester Airport was given permission to build a second runway in 1997 it prompted one of the country's most high-profile environmental protests of the time. Activists from across the country set up camp, built tree houses and a complex network of tunnels in a bid to stop the bulldozers, but after a stand off lasting months they were ultimately evicted and the runway was built. It became operational in 2001 and became the only airport outside of London with two full length runways. Now 25 years on, we look back at the controversy of the project, the impact it has had on the region and its plans for the future. Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, The airport serves over 32m people each year and connects to more than 200 destinations What were the protests about? Large areas of woodland near to the airport would be need to be removed for the runway to be built. After the plans were approved environmental protesters arrived at the site and set up multiple camps. One of the protestors, Martin Porter who was 27 at the time, was among those that dug tunnels at the site. The protesters were soon joined by a environmental activist named Swampy, real name Dan Hooper. "All the time we were there we had the media, we had Swampy, we were able to give our message that this is a terrible idea, 400 acres of green belt disappearing," Porter said. After six months the group were finally evicted. Local resident, Jeff Gazzard, who was also among the protesters, said the national media attention helped to bring environmental issues into the mainstream. "Climate change began to be an issue then, but it wasn't the headlines it is today," he said. "A lot of things have changed in terms of our understanding of the environmental impact of a major airport." Image caption, Martin Porter, aged 27 at the time, dug tunnels during the protests What benefits has the second runway brought? Supporters at the time argued the airport expansion would bring much needed jobs, attract investment, increase tourism, and strengthen Manchester's position internationally. Fast forward 25 years and a report published this week by the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) claims it has done just that. Read the report: A Route to Growth for the North , external The airport now serves 32m people a year with connections to more than 200 destinations and the report estimated the airport's economic impact reached approximately £9.5bn in 2026 - in tourism and business impact - and also supports 117,530 jobs. It says further growth could generate more economic benefits and it has the potential to nearly double passenger numbers. "Airports are not just buildings people pass through as they travel for work or leisure – they are a route to growth for regional economies - economic catalysts integral to our success as an island trading nation," MAG CEO Ken O'Toole said. Image caption, Jeff Gazzard said his concerns about climate change were as strong as ever What is the environmental impact? In 2025, flights from Manchester Airport produced about 3m tonnes of CO2, the equivalent of around 1.5m cars a year and 1.7 times more CO2 than the entire city of Manchester. Manchester Airport says it is "committed to making air travel sustainable for all and working towards national and international decarbonisation targets". "We also safeguard the natural environment and promote the efficient use of resources like water, waste, and energy to increase efficiency and avoid waste." Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig said she was "pushing" the aviation industry "around reducing their carbon footprint". "Similarly we have to make it easier for people to be better connected into jobs and opportunities and as mayor I'm committing to do both," she said. Martin Porter said: "We are going to struggle to meet our net zero contributions and our commitments with existing air travel." Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, The first civil passenger flight, a KLM service to Amsterdam took off from Manchester on 27 June 1938 What are the future plans? candidates.evidence_text: Fans and stars' bow-tie tribute at Jimmy Cricket funeral - BBC News Image caption, Freddie Davis, of Opportunity Knocks fame, was among the mourners By Paul Burnell , North West and Phil Cunliffe , Reporting from at Salford Cathedral Published 21 August 2026 Family, friends, fellow performers and fans of veteran comic Jimmy Cricket have gathered for his funeral. The Northern Ireland-born comedian, real name James Joseph Mulgrew, died on 3 August aged 80. Many mourners at Salford Cathedral responded to his family's request to wear bow ties in a nod to one of his props, while his trademark stage wellies and bowler hat were placed at the cathedral entrance next to a book of condolence. The requiem Mass was led by his son Fr Frankiel Mulgrew, who is based at the cathedral. Image source, PA Image caption, Jimmy Cricket died earlier this month, aged 80 Image caption, Mourners, including family friend Leon Woods, dressed as the comedian, in tribute to his life The comedian, who was born in Cookstown, County Tyrone but later moved to Greater Manchester, became a household name in the 1970s. Among the veteran comedians attending his funeral were Catchphrase host Roy Walker, Crackerjack presenter Stu Francis, Freddie "Parrot face" Davies and Syd Little, half of comedy act Little and Large. Image caption, Two of Jimmy Cricket's daughters, Jamie, 46 and Katie, 41 The star's daughter Katie, who is also a stand-up comic, explained the bow-tie request. "I made a joke and said, 'shall we wear bow ties?' and now my mum is even wearing part of his stage costume," she said. Katie added: "We are heartbroken but he was pure joy and we just wanted to tip our bow ties to him." Image caption, Syd Little, half of Little and Large attended the service His son Fr Mulgrew made mourners laugh at the start of the funeral: "For 10 years I was dad's road manager so I have seen him die before and rise again." He added: "When I entered seminary he said he was willing to sacrifice having grandchildren so it's worked pretty well for him as he got a Papal Knightood and a cheap funeral." Image source, PA Media Image caption, Roy Walker, the original host of the game show Catchphrase John Linehan, a fellow Northern Irish comedian, who performed with Jimmy Cricket in pantomime in Belfast, said he was "superb gentleman, very funny and unvelievably brilliant". Image source, Paul Burnell/BBC Image caption, The star's stage props were displayed at the cathedral Image caption, John Linehan performed with Jimmy Cricket in 170 pantos at Belfast Opera House The father-of-four left school at 16 and spent his summers working as Redcoat camp host at Butlins holiday camps. He went on to work the comedy club scene throughout the 1970s and 1980s, going on to win LWT's Search for a Star talent contest before getting his own ITV show, And There's More, which ran for four seasons. However his son Fr Mulgrew told BBC Radio Manchester his father was joking to the end of his life, even singing a Monty Python song. Image source, Salford Cathedral Image caption, The comedian was awarded a Papal Knightood in 2016 "He was in hospital and called us close to him and we wondered what he would say and he started singing Always Look On The Bright Side Of Life,'" the priest said. Fr Mulgrew added the funeral would be followed by an "open mic" wake, where people could sing and tell jokes. candidates.evidence_text: Man denies charge over Manchester synagogue attack - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The charges are linked to the 2 October 2025 attack By Paul Burnell North West Published 21 August 2026 A man has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the Manchester synagogue attack. Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim appeared before Westminster Magistrates' Court and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. The 49-year-old, of St James Road in Higher Broughton, Salford, spoke only to confirm his name and indicate his plea. He was remanded into custody to appear at at the Old Bailey on 25 September. Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue on 2 October. He then began attacking with a knife, while wearing a fake suicide belt, before being shot dead by police outside the synagogue. First direct charge Sally-Anne Russell, prosecuting, alleged CCTV evidence of conversations between Hakim and Al-Shamie show him "condoning and supporting" the terrorist action. Hakim attended the same mosque as Al-Shamie and travelled in a car with him on various occasions before the attack, which took place on Yom Kippur, one of the holiest day of the Jewish religious calender Cravitz, 66, died from knife wounds inflicted by Al-Shamie while Daulby, 53, was struck by a single gunshot wound to the chest fired by an armed police officer scrambled to the scene in the Crumpsall area of the city. Three other men were treated in hospital for serious injuries. Greater Manchester Police said there have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly". evidence_packet.summary: Damian Woolfenden is accused of posting video footage of a terrorist attacker online
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenager accused of stirring up racial hatred against Jewish people and foreigners and sharing a video of a mass killing online has appeared in court Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide

candidates.lead: A tribunal found Rachel Claire Lemonofides racially discriminated against the patient
candidates.evidence_text: A paramedic has been struck off for telling a woman suffering a stroke to stop acting "like a baby" and accused them of lying about their pain The Healthcare Professionals Tribunal Service heard Rachel Claire Lemonofides made "inappropriate and degrading" comments heard on a 999 call at the woman's home in 2024 It found Lemonofides was guilty of racially motivated discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity and breached professional boundaries The patient underwent emergency surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester, and was diagnosed with a brain bleed and abdominal aortic aneurysm. North West Ambulance Service said all patients were "entitled to be treated with dignity and respect" The service added: "There is no place within our organisation for colleagues who do not uphold those values." The tribunal was told the paramedic was one of a team of two who responded in January 2024 to a 999 call from the patient, who felt a sharp pain in her chest, "which became unbearable"

candidates.lead: Police investigate after the Believe Achieve CIC project was targeted on Monday night
candidates.evidence_text: Site for new Bolton community bike hub 'stormed' by vandals - BBC News Image source, Believe Achieve CIC Image caption, The project was given planning permission in July By Jade Taylorson North West Published 21 August 2026 A site where a new community bike hub is being built to help reduce antisocial behaviour has been vandalised. Police are investigating after the Believe Achieve CIC project in Stoneclough, Bolton, was targeted on Monday night. The bike hub was being built after reports of young people in the area using illegal motorised bikes - and the group aims to give youngsters access to bicycles while teaching road safety and maintenance skills. Tunde Olasupo, project founder, says the site was "stormed" by people who vandalised a surrounding fence and forcibly opened a container that will house the hub. They added there had been opposition to the project, with concerns about further antisocial behaviour. There were also concerns about its location and environmental impact, Olasupo said. 'Upset' "Of course, I'm upset, and when you see something that you've worked hard for deliberately damaged, you're human, it hurts," he told BBC Radio Manchester. He said the site had been targeted before. "The objective is to balance access and community benefit with protecting and enhancing the natural environment, and that's one of the things that we're trying to make very clear to people." Image source, Believe Achieve CIC Image caption, Tunde Olasupo thanked residents who had shown the project support Believe Achieve CIC was set up in memory of Olasupo's son, Kingsley, who died in 2019, with the aim of giving young people opportunities he never got to experience. Despite the damage, Olasupo said he would not give up on the project. "I've learnt something from Kingsley, that everything that happens… there is always a good thing at the end of the road." candidates.lead: Northern Care Alliance has responded to claims raised by an investigation
candidates.evidence_text: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 , external that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims

candidates.evidence_text: A teenager accused of stirring up racial hatred against Jewish people and foreigners and sharing a video of a mass killing online has appeared in court Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide

Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

A court heard they each had two suitcases packed with 20 kilos of cannabis The couriers even had to pay an excess charge at Bangkok Airport to put them in the hold because of their weight, the National Crime Agency said as all 11 people were convicted Bradley Lloyd, 27, of no fixed abode but from Wythenshawe ; Lewis Ross, 35, of Rupert Street, Bolton and Claire McCullough, 36, of Meliden Crescent, Wythenshawe, all pleaded guilty to a charge of knowingly being concerned in the carrying of cannabis with intent to evade prohibiti The three - together with eight others convicted - will be sentenced at a later date

Jennifer Bailey, 48, uses social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to promote her Jennifer grew up in Wigan but now lives in Newton-le-Willows with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. It was during her own teenage years that she developed bunions - hard, bony bumps that form on the inside of the foot at the base of the big toe However, the painful condition also inspired her to start her own business when she was made redundant from her job as Head of Marketing at the Science and Engineering faculty at Salford University "I needed to figure out what I was going to do next because I'd found out I was pregnant at the same time with my youngest daughter," Jennifer told the M.E.N "I had to think about what my next steps were going to be. Originally from Cookstown in Northern Ireland, he had made Rochdale his adopted home in the later years of his life Known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', Cricket became a TV staple in the 80s. In tributes following his passing, Roy Walker described him as a 'sincere wee fella', whilst Christopher Biggins described Cricket as 'unbelievable In a statement, Cricket's family said the artist, who was a devout Catholic, was their 'greatest champion' and that he 'loved us all loudly'. The show ran for four series. Youngest son, a former comedian who became a priest, Father Frankie Mulgrew said the comic had asked for the last rites twice, “almost lik A popular face on television and on the stage, Cricket was given his own show in 1985, named after his iconic catchphrase And There's More. The show ran for four series. He also had a BBC Radio 2 show called Jimmy's Cricket Team, and also regularly made pantomime appearances In 2007, he was one of the comedy icons to appear in the music video for Peter Kay and Matt Lucas' Comic Relief cover of The Proclaimers' hit I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two Greater Manchester towns could be reinstated. The move, being considered by Lancashire councils , would see the previous 236 route brought back into use It would start in the Lancashire town of Rawtenstall and run through to Bolton , stopping off in Ramsbottom along the way. If signed off, the service would begin at the end of November. It would be expected to run every two hours on Mondays through to Saturdays The move to restore the 236 has been welcomed by residents in Ramsbottom, who say they will also benefit from the new connection into Bolton. Currently, those travelling between the two towns have to change buses in Bury One resident said it was ‘great news’, adding they ‘hope it actually happens’ A second person said: “Hopefully this will happen. candidates.evidence_text: Tameside He lured her to her death and left a grieving family without closure Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was preyed upon and murdered - but the man responsible has never said where he left her View 5 Images Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was killed by a vio News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:34, 22 Aug 2026 Ripped apart from their 'lovely girl' by a twisted, remorseless killer, Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin's family have suffered heartache upon heartache. The 24-year-old was reported missing by her grandmother on February 2, 2022 She was one of the people Alisha was closest to in her young life, with the pair having spent a period of time living together. But she had not heard from Alisha in a couple of weeks and was growing concerned about her Greater Manchester Police issued a public missing person's appeal to try and find Alisha on March 1, 2022. Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

candidates.evidence_text: Tony Wilson Even after we lost him Tony Wilson remains a catalyst for debate Peter Hook wants a £250,000 bronze tribute, but as Neal Keeling writes, turning an avant-garde disruptor into a static sculpture has sparked a fierce row across the Irwell. V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

Neal Keeling reports. View 6 News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 22 Aug 2026 His swagger as a cultural pioneer earned him the title of Mr Manchester. But a seven-foot tribute to him could soon rise in Salford Anthony H Wilson, the gifted, influential journalist and music mogul left his mark on Manchester. But he was a proud Salfordian He was born in the city and before studying at Jesus College Cambridge he attended De La Salle Grammar School in Salford. His parents, Sydney and Doris ran a tobacconist shop on Regent Road. As a small child he lived with his parents in a flat above the shop Wilson's maternal family, the Knupfers, had jewellers and watchmaker shops on the same road It has been convincingly argued that the success of Madchester music scene and his Hacienda nightclub was a root cause of the city being able to emerge from post-industrial decline

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Police officer denies PC's claim he described her braided hair as 'like a mop' A misconduct hearing involving seven serving officers and two former officers in Bury is continuing News Paul Britton Reporter 21:05, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bury Polic A police officer facing an allegation he described a female PC colleague's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' told a misconduct hearing she's lying. PC Mohammed Abid said the complainant - a black African-born constable referred to as PC Y - had 'made up' claims that he often s Giving evidence he said he had 'absolutely not' made the comment. "I didn't refer to her hair as a mop," he told the hearing on Friday Opening the case on Monday, Counsel for GMP, Steven Reed, said PC Y wore her hair in braids and it was in braids at the time the comment at the centre of the complaint was made Mr Reed said PC Abid denied making any comment towards her at all, the hearing was told, and claimed he had been the 'victim of racism' A group of Bury-based officers deny breaches of standards in relation to complaints made by the PC, including the mocking and mimicking of her African accent

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Cocky Thailand ‘couriers’ paid extra baggage charges to bring 22 suitcases filled with £13m of cannabis into UK 'My man gonna be on the other side - don't leave the airport until you see him leave' News Paul Britton Reporter 17:27, 21 Aug 2026 V A gang of drug smugglers - including three from Greater Manchester - paid extra baggage charges as they tried to bring 22 suitcases packed with cannabis from Thailand into the UK because they were so heavy Police said the couriers were part of a plot to smuggle cannabis worth £13.8m into the country. A court heard they each had two suitcases packed with 20 kilos of cannabis The couriers even had to pay an excess charge at Bangkok Airport to put them in the hold because of their weight, the National Crime Agency said as all 11 people were convicted Bradley Lloyd, 27, of no fixed abode but from Wythenshawe ; Lewis Ross, 35, of Rupert Street, Bolton and Claire McCullough, 36, of Meliden Crescent, Wythenshawe, all pleaded guilty to a charge of knowingly being concerned in the carrying of cannabis with intent to evade prohibiti The three - together with eight others convicted - will be sentenced at a later date

View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch

candidates.lead: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities.
candidates.evidence_text: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities. View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:11, 21 Aug 2026 A mum who received abuse from online trolls about her foot condition now brings in millions every year with her shoe business. Jennifer Bailey, 48, uses social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to promote her Jennifer grew up in Wigan but now lives in Newton-le-Willows with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. It was during her own teenage years that she developed bunions - hard, bony bumps that form on the inside of the foot at the base of the big toe However, the painful condition also inspired her to start her own business when she was made redundant from her job as Head of Marketing at the Science and Engineering faculty at Salford University "I needed to figure out what I was going to do next because I'd found out I was pregnant at the same time with my youngest daughter," Jennifer told the M.E.N "I had to think about what my next steps were going to be. Was I going to go and get another job with a pregnant belly, or was I going to wait until after I've had the baby and then figure it out?

candidates.lead: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely re
candidates.evidence_text: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely redevelop Bury’s transport interchange could also see new homes built Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has unveiled its ambition to create scores of new homes on land between the interchange and Bury Market. It is now looking for a partner to help it bring its vision to life The scheme could see between 70 and 80 apartments built across an up to six-storey block. While TfGM initially advertised the scheme as fully affordable in its procurement notice, it has now said it is ‘tenure agnostic’ The Local Democracy Reporting Service understands affordable homes are still expected to be the best option for the site, but TfGM is open to a wider range of bids for the contract The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said. Whoever wins the contract would be expected to take responsibility for arranging funding for the scheme, which could include securing grant funding

candidates.evidence_text: Salford LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 13 hours ago Jimmy Cricket funeral RECAP from Salford Cathedral as iconic comedian laid to rest The much-loved comic was known for his bowler hat and his 'and there's more' catchphrase An order of service for the funer The much-loved performer, born James Mulgrew, died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. Originally from Cookstown in Northern Ireland, he had made Rochdale his adopted home in the later years of his life Known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', Cricket became a TV staple in the 80s. In tributes following his passing, Roy Walker described him as a 'sincere wee fella', whilst Christopher Biggins described Cricket as 'unbelievable In a statement, Cricket's family said the artist, who was a devout Catholic, was their 'greatest champion' and that he 'loved us all loudly'. Youngest son, a former comedian who became a priest, Father Frankie Mulgrew said the comic had asked for the last rites twice, “almost lik A popular face on television and on the stage, Cricket was given his own show in 1985, named after his iconic catchphrase And There's More. The show ran for four series. He also had a BBC Radio 2 show called Jimmy's Cricket Team, and also regularly made pantomime appearances In 2007, he was one of the comedy icons to appear in the music video for Peter Kay and Matt Lucas' Comic Relief cover of The Proclaimers' hit I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)

If signed off, the service would begin at the end of November. It would be expected to run every two hours on Mondays through to Saturdays The move to restore the 236 has been welcomed by residents in Ramsbottom, who say they will also benefit from the new connection into Bolton. Currently, those travelling between the two towns have to change buses in Bury One resident said it was ‘great news’, adding they ‘hope it actually happens’ A second person said: “Hopefully this will happen. It's ridiculous that at the moment if you live in the Holcombe Brook area of Ramsbottom you can only go to Bury. With this you can go to Bolton and Rawtenstall.”

Jean Higginbottom has been named as the 73-year-old woman killed in a crash on Manchester Road, near Tintwistle , on Wednesday (August Derbyshire Police says Jean, from Hyde , was driving her silver Renault Clio along Manchester Road when a Nissan Pixo collided with her car close to Millbrook House at 2.30pm that day. Paramedics and police rushed to Jean's aid, but she was sadly pronounced dead at the scene Since Jean was named as the crash victim on Thursday, tributes have poured in on the Manchester Evening News ' Facebook page, from people who knew and loved her. Bea, of Art by Bea Creations in Glossop, posted: "My lovely Godmother, truly one of a kind lady will be missed by many Taz Mass wrote: "Jean was a jolly, kind and caring lady. We always competed against each other with her piebald pony Marie and my piebald cob Murphy, many years ago at New Barn shows. She has been to my house a couple of times too. Not seen her in a number of years but do have fo Rose Elizabeth said: "She was [a] truly amazing person inside and out and a force to be reckoned with! I’m absolutely heartbroken. Rest in peace Jean until we meet again, wait for me with a glass of pinot."

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Trafford's empty wasteland that will soon become the place thousands will call home A 55-bed hotel, new public park, shops and café are also on the cards in Trafford Comments News Hannah Richardson 08:59, 21 Aug 2026 View 3 Images More than 1 Demolition of the former Greater Manchester Police headquarters in Old Trafford is now complete ahead of its major redevelopment After more than a decade and a half of disuse, the nine-acre site will be given a new lease of life through a huge housing project. Around 1,250 homes could be built there, alongside a 55-bed hotel, new public park, shops and café The site previously housed the Chester House GMP headquarters , but has stood empty since the force’s relocation to Newton Heath in 2012 Demolition work began earlier this year, with Trafford council now saying it has been completed. The historic Ellis Llwyd Jones Hall remains standing, however, and is expected to be converted into a community leisure space The moment has been lauded as a ‘milestone’ in the site’s transformation journey. A planning application for the redevelopment was previously expected this summer, but town hall bosses now advise it will come in the autumn

candidates.evidence_text: Boohoo Fashion firm Boohoo fined huge sum by watchdog over misleading pricing practices An investigation took place in France Comments News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 08:17, 21 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Boohoo (Image: PA) Fast fashion firm Boohoo has been fined 2.3 million Euros - around £2 million - by the French consumer watchdog over misleading pricing practices The Directorate-General for Competition, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control (DGCCRF) said Boohoo, part of the recently rebranded Debenhams Group, had given shoppers a false impression about the discounts being offered on the French version of its website Manchester-based Boohoo did not take account of previously applied promotions, or even increased prices before applying a discount, according to the DGCCRF It found 95 per cent of the listings analysed failed to comply with its rules, with 40 per cent offering no price reduction, 7 per cent offering a smaller discount than advertised and 48 per cent actually increasing prices Boohoo also used terms that are banned, such as 'leather' or 'suede' to describe synthetic products, going against French rules on clothes and footwear labelling

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside He lured her to her death and left a grieving family without closure Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was preyed upon and murdered - but the man responsible has never said where he left her View 5 Images Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was killed by a vio News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:34, 22 Aug 2026 Ripped apart from their 'lovely girl' by a twisted, remorseless killer, Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin's family have suffered heartache upon heartache. The 24-year-old was reported missing by her grandmother on February 2, 2022 She was one of the people Alisha was closest to in her young life, with the pair having spent a period of time living together. But she had not heard from Alisha in a couple of weeks and was growing concerned about her Greater Manchester Police issued a public missing person's appeal to try and find Alisha on March 1, 2022. Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

candidates.evidence_text: Tony Wilson Even after we lost him Tony Wilson remains a catalyst for debate Peter Hook wants a £250,000 bronze tribute, but as Neal Keeling writes, turning an avant-garde disruptor into a static sculpture has sparked a fierce row across the Irwell. V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

PC Mohammed Abid said the complainant - a black African-born constable referred to as PC Y - had 'made up' claims that he often s Giving evidence he said he had 'absolutely not' made the comment. candidates.evidence_text: Salford LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 13 hours ago Jimmy Cricket funeral RECAP from Salford Cathedral as iconic comedian laid to rest The much-loved comic was known for his bowler hat and his 'and there's more' catchphrase An order of service for the funer The much-loved performer, born James Mulgrew, died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. Originally from Cookstown in Northern Ireland, he had made Rochdale his adopted home in the later years of his life Known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', Cricket became a TV staple in the 80s. In tributes following his passing, Roy Walker described him as a 'sincere wee fella', whilst Christopher Biggins described Cricket as 'unbelievable In a statement, Cricket's family said the artist, who was a devout Catholic, was their 'greatest champion' and that he 'loved us all loudly'. Youngest son, a former comedian who became a priest, Father Frankie Mulgrew said the comic had asked for the last rites twice, “almost lik A popular face on television and on the stage, Cricket was given his own show in 1985, named after his iconic catchphrase And There's More. The show ran for four series. He also had a BBC Radio 2 show called Jimmy's Cricket Team, and also regularly made pantomime appearances In 2007, he was one of the comedy icons to appear in the music video for Peter Kay and Matt Lucas' Comic Relief cover of The Proclaimers' hit I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)

candidates.evidence_text: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities. View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:11, 21 Aug 2026 A mum who received abuse from online trolls about her foot condition now brings in millions every year with her shoe business. Jennifer Bailey, 48, uses social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to promote her Jennifer grew up in Wigan but now lives in Newton-le-Willows with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. It was during her own teenage years that she developed bunions - hard, bony bumps that form on the inside of the foot at the base of the big toe However, the painful condition also inspired her to start her own business when she was made redundant from her job as Head of Marketing at the Science and Engineering faculty at Salford University "I needed to figure out what I was going to do next because I'd found out I was pregnant at the same time with my youngest daughter," Jennifer told the M.E.N "I had to think about what my next steps were going to be. Was I going to go and get another job with a pregnant belly, or was I going to wait until after I've had the baby and then figure it out?

She pleaded guilty to dangerous driving. She pleaded not guilty to the two arson charges The particulars of the first charge are that on on July 11, 2026 she committed aggravated arson ‘destroying by fire moorland belonging to United Utilities’, being reckless as to whether the life of others was endangered

candidates.lead: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely re
candidates.evidence_text: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely redevelop Bury’s transport interchange could also see new homes built Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has unveiled its ambition to create scores of new homes on land between the interchange and Bury Market. It is now looking for a partner to help it bring its vision to life The scheme could see between 70 and 80 apartments built across an up to six-storey block. While TfGM initially advertised the scheme as fully affordable in its procurement notice, it has now said it is ‘tenure agnostic’ The Local Democracy Reporting Service understands affordable homes are still expected to be the best option for the site, but TfGM is open to a wider range of bids for the contract The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said. Whoever wins the contract would be expected to take responsibility for arranging funding for the scheme, which could include securing grant funding

candidates.lead: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two G
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two Greater Manchester towns could be reinstated. The move, being considered by Lancashire councils , would see the previous 236 route brought back into use It would start in the Lancashire town of Rawtenstall and run through to Bolton , stopping off in Ramsbottom along the way. If signed off, the service would begin at the end of November. It would be expected to run every two hours on Mondays through to Saturdays The move to restore the 236 has been welcomed by residents in Ramsbottom, who say they will also benefit from the new connection into Bolton. Currently, those travelling between the two towns have to change buses in Bury One resident said it was ‘great news’, adding they ‘hope it actually happens’ A second person said: “Hopefully this will happen. It's ridiculous that at the moment if you live in the Holcombe Brook area of Ramsbottom you can only go to Bury. With this you can go to Bolton and Rawtenstall.”

candidates.evidence_text: Boohoo Fashion firm Boohoo fined huge sum by watchdog over misleading pricing practices An investigation took place in France Comments News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 08:17, 21 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Boohoo (Image: PA) Fast fashion firm Boohoo has been fined 2.3 million Euros - around £2 million - by the French consumer watchdog over misleading pricing practices The Directorate-General for Competition, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control (DGCCRF) said Boohoo, part of the recently rebranded Debenhams Group, had given shoppers a false impression about the discounts being offered on the French version of its website Manchester-based Boohoo did not take account of previously applied promotions, or even increased prices before applying a discount, according to the DGCCRF It found 95 per cent of the listings analysed failed to comply with its rules, with 40 per cent offering no price reduction, 7 per cent offering a smaller discount than advertised and 48 per cent actually increasing prices Boohoo also used terms that are banned, such as 'leather' or 'suede' to describe synthetic products, going against French rules on clothes and footwear labelling

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan residents hail extraordinary victory after council U-turns on masterplan - but this was 'just one battle' Bridgewater West has been removed from a local plan - meaning a scheme to turn it into a giant Wigan business park could be scrapped Campaigners say ‘the fight isn’t over’ after Wigan Council U-turned on plans to free up former greenbelt land in Astley for a huge business park Bridgewater West was tipped to become the home of around 540,000 sq ft of ‘employment space’ under the council’s Local Plan. Peel Group, which owns the land, planned to turn the area into a ‘ campus style’ business park, alongside new homes and a Park and Ride Campaigners have opposed the scheme from the start , arguing the open fields separating Astley and Boothstown are ‘vital’ to the local community and wildlife as well as protection from flooding. After a year of disputes, Wigan bosses have now rowed back on the scheme Four ‘controversial’ sites will be removed from the local plan. The document was due to be greenlit for public consultation at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, August 27. However now, The Bell, north of Junction 26, the Moss Industrial Estate extension, a pocket of land West of Win Joanna Allsopp, a high school teacher campaigning for the protection of the land , said the shift was a ‘positive step’

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.evidence_text: Thursday 23 July 2026 at 4:58pm King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court. Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

candidates.evidence_text: Monday 13 July 2026 at 3:43pm Play Brightcove video Sarah and husband Martin has been speaking to ITV Granada Reports’ Emma Sweeney A breast cancer patient from Greater Manchester says she’s devastated and angry that a drug that she believes could extend her life is still not available on the NHS in England Sarah Barchetti, who has been living with secondary breast cancer for seven years, has been treated at The Christie hospital in Manchester throughout her illness. But now, as NHS treatment options dwindle, Sarah has turned to fundraising for private care Sarah said: “It blew our world apart,” recalling her diagnosis in 2019 She added: “I’ve lived with it now for seven years. I’m eternally grateful to The Christie, but we’ve come to a point now where they can’t offer me anything else under the NHS. My team are as frustrated as I am.” Sarah believes the drug Enhertu could help her, but while it is available to NHS patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer in Scotland, it is not yet offered in England

A trader who picks up wholesale customers in Rotterdam, or starts posting orders to Dublin, finds the same signal now working against the traffic they want, and no setting anywhere undoes it

candidates.evidence_text: Earlier this year, the designer Faheem Aftab walked into a hotel for the homeless. He was its newest resident Dear readers — happy Friday, for a start. Today’s piece is a Jack Dulhanty classic: a moving portrait of a man who rose through the world of architecture to become a self-made multi-millionaire, only to find himself in homeless accommodation earlier this year. So what went wrong? There were balloons, flowers, cards and a cake made by the home’s head chef Mary, 98, from Gateshead, and Peter, 97, from Newark, met at the Oxford Galleries dance hall in Newcastle and married at St Chad’s Church in Gateshead. They later lived in Nottingham and Ireland, raised three children, and now have six grandchildren and three great-grandchildren Mary and Peter said: “We loved the whole day, especially being able to celebrate with our children. The cake was amazing; having our wedding picture on the top was a lovely touch.” Their secret after more than seven decades? “Being supportive.”

candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

candidates.evidence_text: Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide The teenager is charged with three counts of publishing threatening written material stirring up racial hatred, one relating to foreigners and one to Jewish people

candidates.evidence_text: Food lovers are in for a treat as Bolton Food and Drink Festival returns with hundreds of traders offering an incredible range of food, drink, artisan products and gifts from across the globe Festival-goers will be able to sample flavours from every corner of the world, from authentic Greek gyros, Turkish shawarma and Thai street food to Portuguese pastries, Italian pasta, Caribbean dishes and Indian curries Traders including Greek Street Food by the Malaka Brothers, Istanbul’s Kitchen, Thai 2 Go, Happy Dumpling 365 and Dobra Kitchen are among those set to bring international flavours to Bolton town centre Bolton Food and Drink Festival offers something for every taste and budget Visitors with a sweet tooth will also find plenty to enjoy, with festival favourites including Fifi's Cheesecakes, Nutella House, Choc-O-Licious, Love Crepes, Pit Stop Donut King and several artisan fudge makers The festival will also showcase a wealth of independent food producers, offering everything from locally produced honey and handmade cheeses to artisan breads, specialist sauces and gourmet preserves. Among the traders taking part are Bright Meadows Honey, Great British Cheese Co

Download A safe and suitable home is the foundation of a good quality of life Whether it is helping young people take their first step onto the housing ladder, supporting older residents to live independently, or improving existing neighbourhoods, housing plays a vital role in creating thriving communities That's why Bury Council is asking tenants, residents, businesses and community groups to have their say on its draft Housing Strategy 2026-2036 which will help shape housing priorities across the borough for the next decade Bury Council has published its draft strategy document and is asking people across the borough what they think before it is finalised The consultation opens today Thursday 13 August and runs for twelve weeks, closing on 5 November 2026

I welcome that “But big infrastructure projects can take years. candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Welcome to The Bolly-woods, where the dancing is non-stop, the drama is bigger than your aunties, and the romance is straight out of a filmi blockbuster! Meet Surinder, sweet, strong, and stuck in a never-ending chore list thanks to her two Insta-fame obsessed stepsisters, Lovely and Bubbly. Her only real support? Book your tickets now, before midnight strikes! A delightful blend of storytelling, music, dance and humour. A fine example of the way diversity enriches our culture. The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

candidates.evidence_text: Sat 22nd Aug, 2026 - Sun 23rd Aug, 2026 - Torr Vale Mill Open Fire Dining Club: Pho Cue x Tartuffe Torr Vale Mill, Torrvale Rd, High Peak SK22 3HS Sat 22nd Aug, 2026 - Sun 23rd Aug, 2026 4pm - 9:30pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Pho Cue are leaving Chinatown behind for the weekend and heading to the edge of the Peak District, joining Tartuffe for the next Open Fire Dining Club One of those Manchester restaurants that doesn’t really need much selling, Pho Cue has built a loyal following for Vietnamese cooking that’s informal, generous and consistently very good. Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, while it remains a r For Open Fire Dining Club, the team are taking things somewhere slightly different. Across 22 and 23 August , they’ll work with Tartuffe on a menu that brings together traditional Vietnamese fire cooking, Cue’s more modern approach and some of the French influence that still runs The menu starts with a Carlingford oyster dressed with fermented mango , mint and smoked soy, followed by cá tái chanh made with chalk stream trout, fruit, mustard and rong nho — the tiny sea grapes found along Vietnam’s coastline There’s lobster congee too , alongside a small tasting-menu take on lobster and beef pho. It would be strange to invite Pho Cue and not let pho make an appearance somewhere

Twenty traders have been sel The judging panel includes BBC Radio Manchester Breakfast Show host Joe McGrath , creator of ‘Filler’ zine Holly Temple and chef Sam Buckley , of acclaimed Stockport restaurant ‘Where The Light Gets In’, which has a Green Michelin Star. They will decide which trader goes forward As well as so many delicious food choices on offer, the event will also feature live music and children’s activities throughout the afternoon making this the ideal family-friendly day out. Visitors are strongly encouraged to come along to eat, drink and vote !

candidates.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

candidates.lead: Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities.
candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. candidates.evidence_text: The Science and Industry Museum has unveiled a special Pride programme coinciding with Manchester’s famous celebration of inclusivity this August Spanning talks, newly displayed objects and creative workshops, the Museum’s Pride schedule will kick off on Mon 24 Aug, running through the duration of the festivities until Mon 31 Aug Central to the programme will be a series of Spotlight Talks that explore and celebrate the life and legacy of LGBTQ+ hero Alan Turing. Widely recognised as one of the founding fathers of computer science, Turing’s wartime codebreaking contributions helped save an immeasurable nu Led by the museum’s friendly Spotlight Volunteers in the Revolution Manchester Gallery, these talks will take place Mon 24 Aug and Mon 31 Aug at 1.45pm and 2.45pm, and on Sat 29 Aug at 11.15am, 12.15pm and 1.45pm Alongside the Spotlight Talks, there’ll be opportunities to discover more about Turing’s impact through newly installed objects and stories which will be displayed alongside the iconic Manchester ‘Baby’ computer These include Baiba Auria’s rainbow portrait, which celebrates Turing’s iconic status among the LGBTQIA+ community in Manchester, and a special £50 note featuring the visionary mathematician’s face

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way
